messages:
ashok: quick question — for private deployments are we leaning toward short-circuit controlplane (direct CP->DP inside customer VPC) or relay-mode (regional relay/proxy in our VPC)?

maria: short take: short-circuit reduces egress + hops but bumps customer trust surface and ops complexity. relay-mode centralizes auth and makes rollout easier.

kevin: timeline constraint: customers asking for Private with <10ms added tail latency for controlplane calls. relay-mode adds ~15-40ms depending on region.

olga: @kevin can you paste the perf numbers from the last test?

kevin: sure — synthetic: relay via regional-proxy avg RTT 22ms (p95 48ms). direct-peering inside VPC avg RTT 8ms (p95 14ms). numbers for small controlplane RPCs (auth + config fetch).

maria: thanks. latency aside, short-circuit means we need a minimal controlplane agent in-customer that handles cert negotiation, health, and fallback routing. that's a non-trivial lifecycle + security boundary.

ashok: security angle: with short-circuit we still MUST maintain controlplane identity assertions. I prefer mutual TLS with customer-side mTLS termination to limit long-lived credentials in our controlplane.

olga: agreed. But client-side mTLS implies we need to rotate certs inside their VPC and support push/pull variants. Ops surface increases.

kevin: also note metrics and tracing continuity — relay-mode gives us single point to sample/tracing logs without distributing collectors. short-circuit requires collector-sidecar or remote-forwarding which customer may block.

maria: tradeoff summary I posted in the RFC followup doc (link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/priv-net-shortcircuit). High-level: short-circuit = best perf, more customer ops and cert mgmt; relay = simpler rollout, central observability, easier canary.

tom: customer ask — regulated fintech needs no egress to public subnets at all. relay-mode would involve traffic exiting customer VPC to our relay unless we put relay inside customer's infra (which defeats relay benefits).

ashok: we can offer three modes: 1) relay (default), 2) short-circuit (agent+peering), 3) managed-relay-in-customer (deployed into their account via infra-as-code). Each has different SLA/cost.

olga: that seems reasonable. We need clear interface contract for short-circuit agent: minimal API surface, auth handshake, health probes, local routing table requirements, and fallback to relay.

maria: propose an interface: agent exposes a local socket and forwards CP RPCs; controlplane calls are signed with ephemeral cert established via an onetime OIDC flow; fallback flag in config points to relay endpoint. Keep proto backwards compatible.

kevin: +1 on ephemeral certs. Implementation note: use SPOKE model — agent does TLS-terminating, verifies our CP CA, and stores ephemeral creds in KMS inside their account if provided.

ashok: ops concerns: when short-circuit is enabled, our ability to patch controlplane quickly is reduced because we can't update inside customer VPC. Need a fast rollback path (force-fallback to relay).

maria: implement guardrail: agent must support 'force-fallback' via signed command from CP that flips traffic to relay within 5s. Also periodic heartbeat so CP can detect silent failures and auto-fallback.

tom: question about DNS: short-circuit currently requires customers to route cp.<region>.redwood via route table or private hosted zone. Do we allow hostless IP routing (ENI-based) or require private-zone delegation?

olga: prefer private-hosted-zone delegation for TLS SNI continuity and cert validation. ENI-based IPs are brittle for cross-account migrations and scaling.

kevin: noted. Also batching: short-circuit reduces per-request kernel hops but hampers our batching opportunities (we rely on central relay to consolidate). For throughput-critical customers, we'll need local batching inside the agent.

maria: action items: 1) define agent RPC API (ashok + olga), 2) design ephemeral cert flow + KMS integration (kevin + ashok), 3) fallback semantics doc + health probes (maria), 4) cost/SLA tiers for three modes (tom).

ashok: I'll start a spike for agent API with a minimal gRPC surface and health endpoints. Will include code sketch:
```
service AgentControl {
  rpc Heartbeat(HeartbeatReq) returns (HeartbeatResp);
  rpc FetchConfig(FetchReq) returns (Config);
  rpc ForceFallback(ForceReq) returns (Ack);
}
```

maria: Cool — in the RFC followup we should enumerate failure scenarios: network partition, cert compromise, CP region outage, and agent compromise. For each map mitigations and diagnostic signals.

olga: ops note: logging forwarders must support sampling/masking PII; customers will often block broad log egress. Add a 'telemetry opt-in' toggle for short-circuit.

kevin: timeline proposal: 2-week spike -> demo in staging -> customer beta for 1-2 customers -> GA in 3 months if no major issues.

tom: fine with that. I'll start pricing modeling for an add-on 'short-circuit private' with extra support SLA.

maria: final call: we're not making a hard decision now. consensus: support relay-mode as GA default; implement short-circuit as an opt-in advanced mode with strong guardrails and fallback. I'll file a short RFC amendment and PR the followup checklist. :white_check_mark:

ashok: +1

olga: +1

kevin: +1

sre-bot: reminder — created followup ticket INFRA-4821 for agent spike and assigned to @ashok.
